divergences: API: LEADERBOARD_POLICY and leaderboardFetch (AlienClaw-specific) are not exported; all other exports (FetchPolicy, ResolvedAddress, DEFAULT_PROTOCOLS, MAX_REDIRECTS, isBlockedHost, validateResolvedAddresses, hardenedFetch) are identical, except that the staged FetchPolicy has the optional resolve field and exports the type Resolver (connection pinning, below). No runtime export was added.

Block list: CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 was already blocked in-tree, and the 2026-11-26 NAT64 change was made in both modules. The staged copy additionally blocks (staged only, 2026-11-26; shared vector corpus groups g6/g7/g11 and meta-azure-wireserver): 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001:0::/32 and site-local fec0::/10 whole in isBlockedIpv6 (matching the Python package, which blocks all three whole), and the Azure WireServer address 168.63.129.16 in isBlockedIpv4 (so the NAT64 decode blocks 64:ff9b::a83f:8110 too). In-tree allows all of them. These are DECISION divergences: test/parity-in-tree.test.ts declares exactly these ranges (inDeclaredRange), asserts that every corpus and property input in them is blocked by staged and allowed by in-tree, that each still differs today, and that nothing else differs.

Non-behavioural: unused node:http and node:https imports removed (node:http/node:https are now used by src/pinned-request.ts); header comment rewritten (AlienClaw consumer list dropped; the in-tree claim that resolver-inconsistency attacks are impossible corrected); one section comment reworded. Function bodies were verbatim until connection pinning (below); the classifier bodies (isBlockedHost, validateResolvedAddresses and helpers) still are.

Tests: ported ssrf-vectors fixes the in-tree '[::])' typo (it passed only via fail-closed parsing) and replaces four vacuous obfuscated-IPv4 assertions with real new URL() canonicalisation; the two expect(true) jail construction notes are not ported.

Tests: test/hardening.test.ts is the in-tree test/net/hardened-fetch-hardening.test.ts without its LEADERBOARD_POLICY / leaderboardFetch block; test/hardened-fetch.test.ts flips the NAT64 and body-read KNOWN GAPS into 'fixed gaps' and expects timeoutMs 0 to be an invalid policy.

2026-11-26 security fixes, applied identically to src/alienclaw/net/hardened-fetch.ts and the staged copy (findings from docs/salvage/SANDBOX-SECURITY-REVIEW.md): SR-05 FetchPolicy is validated before any I/O (timeoutMs integer 1..2147483647, maxBytes integer 0..268435456, maxRedirects integer 0..20 defaulting to MAX_REDIRECTS, protocols an array of strings, allowedHosts a Set; anything else throws TypeError 'Invalid FetchPolicy: ...'; this also fixes SR-11 timer overflow); SR-07 one AbortController deadline covers DNS, connect, headers and the full body read across all hops; SR-12 (NAT64 part) 64:ff9b::/96 is blocked when its embedded IPv4 is blocked, and 64:ff9b:1::/48 is blocked whole. 6to4, Teredo and fec0::/10 stayed open in-tree (closed in the staged copy only, see the Block list line); DNS pinning (SR-04) remains open in-tree and is closed in the staged copy only (next line).

connection pinning added (staged only, 2026-11-26): SR-04 / extraction-plan gate G2. src/alienclaw/net/hardened-fetch.ts is unchanged (its source_blob above still matches). hardenedFetch no longer calls fetch(): each hop resolves once (dns.promises.lookup(host, {all:true}) or the new optional FetchPolicy.resolve hook, validated as a function like the other fields; hook answers must be an array of {address: string, family: number}), validates every answer with the unchanged validateResolvedAddresses plus a net.isIP canonical-form check, and sends one GET through the new internal src/pinned-request.ts: node:http/node:https to the original hostname (Host header, SNI and certificate check keep the name) with a lookup option that returns only the validated addresses (all:true form included) and a fresh keepAlive:false Agent per request (no socket reuse, proxy env ignored). The transport reproduces fetch()'s request headers (except connection: close), content decoding, bad-port list, credentials TypeError, 'fetch failed' / 'terminated' error shapes and null-body statuses; IPv6-literal URLs are now resolved without brackets (fixes SR-09); redirect bodies are cancelled before the next hop. Tests: the decision tests stub the internal transport.request seam instead of globalThis.fetch (test/hardened-fetch.test.ts, test/hardening.test.ts, test/ssrf-vectors.test.ts, test/cgnat.test.ts; the DNS-rebinding KNOWN GAP is flipped into 'fixed gaps'), test/parity-in-tree.test.ts stubs the transport for the staged module and fetch for the in-tree one with the same response queue, and the new test/pinning.test.ts covers rebinding (socket target asserted), refusal before connect, Host/SNI/certificate, pinned redirect hops and fetch() parity of the transport. See README 'Connection pinning'.

source_commit is still the original copy point. source_blob for test/hardening.test.ts is the post-fix in-tree blob (git hash-object), which was not yet committed when it was written. source_blob for src/hardened-fetch.ts is 862591bb (in-tree commit d18c5c5d), refreshed 2026-11-26 when that commit was ported (next line).

Port 0 (staged only, 2026-11-26; shared vector corpus port-zero): validateUrl refuses an explicit URL port outside 1-65535 with 'Port rejected: <port> is not a port from 1 to 65535', after the protocol check and before the literal check and DNS. WHATWG keeps ':0' and node:http reads port 0 as the default, so the pinned transport used to dial 80/443. In-tree hands the URL to fetch(). A DECISION divergence, declared end-to-end in test/parity-in-tree.test.ts.

Ported in-tree commit d18c5c5d ('only the deadline's own abort is reported as a timeout'), adapted: the deadline aborts the controller with its own Error, `expired` rejects with that same Error, and the outer catch rethrows it only when signal.aborted AND isDeadlineError(err). In-tree's isDeadlineError checks err === deadline, err.cause === deadline and err.name === 'AbortError'; the staged one walks the cause chain (up to 4 levels) for the same two conditions, because the pinned transport reports a body broken by the abort as TypeError('terminated', { cause: <Node AbortError> }) (pinnedRequest itself rejects an aborted request with signal.reason, which is the deadline). Regression test: test/timeout-masking.test.ts, adapted from in-tree test/net/hardened-fetch-timeout-masking.test.ts (stubs transport.request instead of fetch; adds a resolve-hook case, a non-abort transport error case and a terminated-body control).

Tests (staged only, 2026-11-26): new test/corpus-gaps.test.ts covers the 6to4, Teredo, fec0::/10, WireServer and port-0 changes; test/hardened-fetch.test.ts flips its 6to4 and fec0 KNOWN GAPS into 'fixed gaps'.
